characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: MatSAM (based on Segment Anything Model, SAM)
characterization_methods.key_findings: MatSAM accurately recognizes all phases (γ', TCP and impurities); the γ' phase key-structure binary mask appears as dense white speckle
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: training-free (no manual annotations); these image samples are not provided with corresponding annotations
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify and extract the γ' phase microstructure in NBS-3 micrograph without manual annotation
characterization_methods.technique: Microstructure image segmentation using MatSAM (Materials Segment Anything Model, training-free visual large model)

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: structure-aware prompt points (ROI points from rule-based pre-segmentation merged with grid points); hierarchical crops of 1/1, 1/4 and 1/16 image size with default overlap ratio 0.5
computational_details.simulation_method: MatSAM (training-free microstructure segmentation based on the Segment Anything Model, SAM)
computational_details.software_used: MatSAM framework; validation experiments conducted using PyTorch 1.13.1 library
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: NBS-3 image has no annotations; validation is qualitative (visual comparison of Image, Overlay and Key structure columns in Fig.10)

defects.type: impurities (deeply dark in color, distinctly larger in area)

phases_present.morphology: small light grey areas (b0102); Fig.10 shows a fine globular/network phase in a lighter matrix

structures.overall_structure: γ' phase present as small light grey areas (key object of analysis); impurities deeply dark in color and distinctly larger in area also present

unmapped_findings: NBS-3 (γ' phase) is one of six additional micrographs used in the extended experiments of MatSAM; these image samples are not provided with corresponding annotations.
NBS-3 micrographs also contain TCP phase (fine needle-like), which is the key object of the sibling sample NBS-3 (TCP phase), shown as panel (b) of Fig.10.
The raw-image acquisition technique (e.g., OM/SEM/XCT) for NBS-3 is not reported in the paper; NBS-1/NBS-2 of the same alloy family were obtained by SEM.
No quantitative segmentation metrics (IoU/F1/Recall) are reported for NBS-3 because the extended-experiment images lack ground-truth annotations.
